abstract: Keyword difficulty (KD) is a score, usually 0 to 100, that estimates how hard it is to reach page one of Google for a search term. Tools such as Semrush and Ahrefs calculate it from the strength of the pages that already rank, so scores differ by tool. Use it to compare keywords, then read the real results page to decide.

mainEntity.name: What is keyword difficulty in SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keyword difficulty is a score, usually from 0 to 100, that estimates how hard it is to rank on the first page of Google for a keyword. Higher means more competition. It is calculated by SEO tools, not by Google.

mainEntity.name: What is a good keyword difficulty score?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your site. New sites do best with scores of 0 to 30. Sites with more links and trust can aim for 31 to 60 or higher. Check the keywords you already rank for to find your own reach.

Each tool studies the pages that rank in the top 10 and scores how strong they are, often using backlinks, domain and page authority, content quality and search results features. The formulas are private and differ by tool.
It is a useful estimate, not a promise. Tools disagree, many lean heavily on links and none know your own site. Use it to make a shortlist and then read the real results.

mainEntity.name: Is a low keyword difficulty always better?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Some easy keywords bring visitors who will never buy. Pick keywords that are winnable and relevant to your business, and check the search intent.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between keyword difficulty and search volume?

acceptedAnswer.text: Search volume is how many times a month people search for a term. Keyword difficulty is how hard it is to rank for it. You need both to choose a keyword.

mainEntity.name: Can I check keyword difficulty for free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Free checkers show a score and volume for a few searches a day. You can also read the top 10 results yourself and use Google Search Console to find phrases you almost rank for.

mainEntity.name: How do I rank for a high-difficulty keyword?

acceptedAnswer.text: Build a group of related pages, make the main page clearly better than those that rank, earn links from relevant sites, and expect it to take months. Start with easier related keywords to build trust.
Long-tail keywords are longer, more specific phrases. They usually have lower difficulty and clearer intent, which makes them a good starting point for newer sites.

mainEntity.name: How often should I recheck keyword difficulty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every three to six months, and before you update an older page. Results and scores change as new pages are published and links are earned.
No. Keyword difficulty is an estimate created by SEO tools. Google does not publish a difficulty score. Semrush says on its own page that it is not an official Google metric.

mainEntity.name: Why is keyword difficulty different in Ahrefs and Semrush?

acceptedAnswer.text: They measure different things. Ahrefs scores referring domains to the top 10 pages. Semrush blends referring domains, authority, link type, search volume and search result features. Compare keywords inside one tool, not across tools.
